short: Isolated extraoral inputs (M05) and face Cutout (M03) are ahead, but the face-over-mouth gain fails on LRW, Cutout is untested on mouths, and GRID 2.9% only ties LCANet.
position: The paper [@zhang2020beyond] changes the input region (M05) and the training augmentation (M03). Both are ahead at the time: none of 162 prior decoders feeds isolated extraoral regions or masked input patches, and upper-face and cheek inputs score far above chance on LRW, LRW-1000 and GRID. The whole-face advantage over the mouth holds on LRW-1000 and GRID but not on LRW, and face-versus-mouth comparisons predate it in video-to-speech [@ephrat2017vid2speech]. Cutout is never applied to mouth crops, so its gain is not tied to extraoral cues. The GRID state-of-the-art claim ties LCANet at 2.9% WER [@xu2018lcanet]; later work returned to lip crops [@feng2020pains] and reaches 93.2% on LRW [@ahn2024syncvsr].
